overview: The Scottish Highlands and Isle of Skye feature a street food scene centered on fresh seafood and local game. Visitors find wooden shacks serving fresh langoustines and scallops right on the harbor, alongside monthly farmers' markets selling venison and haggis in the warmer months.
months: Most coastal food shacks close entirely for the winter. The Inverness Farmers' Market still operates on the first Saturday of the month, but outdoor eating is limited to a few hardy vendors selling hot Cullen skink or haggis.

Shoulder season brings unpredictable weather, but major seafood stalls usually open for the season in April and wind down in October. Expect shorter hours and occasional closures on windy or rainy days.

The coastal seafood shacks operate at full capacity. Places like The Seafood Shack in Ullapool and The Oyster Shed in Carbost serve fresh langoustines, crab, and oysters outdoors. Inverness Farmers' Market runs with its highest number of vendors selling local cheeses and venison.

overview: Sedona's small street food scene centers on the Sedona Community Farmers Market, which runs through the warmer months and offers produce, tamales, and baked goods. A handful of food trucks operate around the city offering casual bites like tacos and Navajo fry bread.
months: The farmers market shifts to its winter schedule and location. Fresh produce vendors thin out, though hot food stalls and baked goods remain. Cooler weather makes eating at outdoor food trucks pleasant.
